emily (eng-ml): heads up — bringing up Stellar-9B-alt (int4 per-channel) on canary. Early wins on throughput but hit two problems: (1) summarization eval quality dropped vs fp16, (2) intermittent OOMs during warmup that smell like memory fragmentation. Posting quick notes + logs, anyone seen this combo?

raj (eng-ml): can you share the quant config + sample eval diffs?

emily (eng-ml): config pasted below — using group_size=128 initially. eval set is our news-sum-dev (2000 docs).
```json
{"model":"stellar-9b-alt","quant":"int4_perchannel","bits":4,"group_size":128,"prefetch":true,"batch_size":8,"max_new_tokens":256}
```

sophia (runtime): alloc trace / OOM snippet? also did you run with mem_compact enabled?

emily (eng-ml): log excerpt from warmup run:
```
[2026-03-18T14:02:11Z] ERROR OOM allocate 536870912 bytes
stack: runtime/kv_cache::grow -> allocator::alloc
stats: total_alloc=1.2GB free_fragments=23 avg_fragment=16MB
runtime_flags: mem_compact=false prealloc_kv=0
```

jordy (prod-ml): yep that looks like fragmentation — lots of small free fragments and mem_compact off. For int4 per-channel we also see bigger transient KV growth during beam/ensemble prompts. Two quick knobs: drop batch -> 4 and flip mem_compact=true; also try group_size=64 for quant.

benchbot: quick perf snapshot (canary runs):
- int4_perchannel bsz=8 max_new=256: p50=85ms p95=380ms tokens/s=280 cost/1M=$2.30
- int4_perchannel bsz=4 max_new=128: p50=60ms p95=230ms tokens/s=220 cost/1M=$2.00
Full dashboard: https://bench.redwood.internal/stellar9b/317408 (canary)

raj (eng-ml): quality numbers? group128 vs group64 vs fp16?

emily (eng-ml): summarization eval (news-sum-dev):
- fp16 baseline: ROUGE-L=38.7
- int4 group128: ROUGE-L=36.2 (-2.5)
- int4 group64: ROUGE-L=36.8 (-1.9)
So group64 recovers ~0.6 ROUGE-L and seems worth trying.

sophia (runtime): operational plan: 1) enable mem_compact and run warmup x1k examples, 2) set prealloc_kv=200MB to reduce churn, 3) canary rollout with bsz=4 max_new_tokens=128 + group_size=64. Also note allocator differences — jemalloc tends to have fewer small-frag issues than tcmalloc for our access patterns.

emily (eng-ml): implemented canary config: `group_size=64, batch_size=4, max_new_tokens=128, mem_compact=true, prealloc_kv=200MB`. Starting small canary (10 pods) now. Will run the full eval and warmup script.

benchbot: initial canary metrics (first 500 requests): no OOMs, p50=62ms p95=248ms, tokens/s=210, cost/1M=$2.05. Telemetry link: https://bench.redwood.internal/stellar9b/canary-317408

emily (eng-ml): eval after 1k warmups: ROUGE-L=36.6, no OOMs during warmup, p95 ~245ms. Still a bit below fp16 but cost delta is ~4-6x better.

jordy (prod-ml): recommendation: set model card defaults -> quant: int4_perchannel group64, batch_default=4, max_new_tokens_default=128, runtime_hint=mem_compact=true, prealloc_kv=200MB. Start slow A/B with small % traffic and monitor eval regressions.

raj (eng-ml): also add a test to our onboarding harness that runs a quick mem-frag smoke (warmup + kv-grow) so future models catch this pattern early.

emily (eng-ml): done — pushed model card + defaults and added the mem-frag smoke to the onboarding CI. Will keep canary at 10 pods for 24h. Thanks everyone :rocket:

sophia (runtime): nice. if anything reappears ping me and we can try jemalloc build or a background compaction pass between requests.

emily (eng-ml): will do — closing for now, will report back after 24h canary. :white_check_mark:
